details:
We are Team Tuva from Sivas University of Science and Technology, named after Turkey's second astronaut, Tuva Cihangir Atasever, and the fertile Valley of Tuva. Our project, Veysel, is an interactive decision-support platform that turns NASA Earth observations into crop rotation strategies farmers can understand and trust. Inspired by the harsh winters of Sivas and folk poet Âşık Veysel’s devotion to the earth, we go to space not to turn our backs on the soil, but to come home better.

Farmers face mounting uncertainty from frost, erratic rainfall, drought, heat stress, and soil erosion. While NASA satellites (SMAP, GPM, ECOSTRESS, Landsat/MODIS, SRTM) capture regional trends, only the farmer knows localized ground truths like pesticide drift from neighboring fields or poor drainage spots. Veysel bridges this gap through four transparent steps—Observe, Fuse, Score, and Explain—combining satellite data, soil layers, and the farmer's 1-to-5 field observations into an explainable multi-criteria scoring engine ($\text{Score} = w_1\text{Water} + w_2\text{Soil} + w_3\text{Erosion} + w_4\text{Market}$).

Designed for accessibility, Veysel features a bilingual (TR/EN) interface with Simple and Advanced modes, equipment/market constraint filters, and a HayDay-style visual simulation where sliders like "what if rainfall drops by 20%?" dynamically update crop health and scores. Beyond recommendations, Veysel builds agricultural literacy through gamified educational modules—interactive swipe cards simulating drought, rust disease, and monoculture risks where crops visibly grow or wilt based on farmer choices. For real-world collaboration, an integrated Agronomist Expert Module lets farmers share field photos and rotation plans with local specialists for pesticide resistance and dosage advice, supported by a dual-mode AI Assistant & WhatsApp bridge featuring NASA space-agriculture stories. Ultimately, Veysel provides decision support, not decision making—empowering humans to make the final call.
